already-have.reason: Not fully implemented and no recorded owner decision contradicts it. Verified in-repo: (1) no timing canary / TimedWindow exists — every DWT CYCCNT use is bench instrumentation (bench_masked_sha.rs, splash_test.rs, lcd_nv3007.rs:849-863, main_sau_pure_tests.rs:1098) and `secure/src/fi.rs` (372 lines) / `pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs` have no timer-window primitive; CfiCounter (fi.rs:199-239) is control-flow-only as the proposal states. (2) `secure/src/hw/rcc.rs` `try_pll_160mhz` (lines ~185-243) writes PLL1CFGR/PLL1DIVR and only spins on PLL1RDY/SWS — there is no post-switch re-read of CFGR1/PLL1CFGR/PLL1DIVR against the constants, no sentinel, no wait_random. (3) `secure/src/sau.rs` F6 verifier is a single plain `read()` per register (lines 586-590 for TZSC SECCFGR1-3, 726 for AIRCR, 743-744 for CSLCKR/TZSC_CR) with no `wait_random` before it and no `read_volatile_voted` — grep for wait_random/read_volatile_voted in sau.rs and rcc.rs returns nothing. The proposal is partially anticipated and tracked by several open issues (see corrections) but none of them covers the timing-window or jitter-then-readback mechanism itself.
already-have.corrections: Partial precedents and deltas the proposal should absorb: (a) `fi::read_volatile_voted` (secure/src/fi.rs:153) already exists — part (3) is a wiring change, not a new primitive. (b) The FSBL already has the two-pass sentinel-gated readback pattern the proposal asks for, in `fsbl/src/optbytes.rs:79-85` `persistent_confirmed_match` (two `check_true_into_sentinel` passes with `scrub_sentinel_register` between) — but it is OR-of-two-passes (halt only on persistent mismatch, 2026-07-23 coordinator refinement, availability-biased), so the secure-side SAU/GTZC/AIRCR double pass must decide AND vs OR semantics explicitly rather than copy it. (c) `fsbl/src/fi.rs:26-37` confirms the FSBL has no TRNG (`rng_byte` returns a fixed byte), so 'mirror in the FSBL once it has a TRNG' is correctly gated; `fsbl/src/clock.rs` never configures the PLL (HSI16 only, SWS-derived) so the RCC readback there is moot. (d) CONFLICT with current code, not an owner decision: `secure/src/main.rs:4263-4273` deliberately enables DWT CYCCNT for the NON-SECURE world ('so the non-secure world can measure timing (e2e benchmarks, companion latency logging)' with DSCSR.CDS) — a TimedWindow on DWT would be NS-resettable; the proposal should use the already-secured TIM2/TIM3 (sau.rs secures both so NS cannot stop them) or re-secure DWT and drop the NS benchmark hook. (e) Hardware side partly covered: `secure/src/hw/tamp.rs` already enables ITAMP9 (crypto-peripheral fault) and ITAMP3 (LSE CSS) — but SYSCLK is HSI16→PLL1 with no HSE, so RCC CSS does not apply to the core clock and ITAMP3 only covers LSE; the software window is the only core-clock-glitch detector available. (f) Open issues that overlap: #80 F3 RCC_SECCFGR and #269 tz-3 (secure the RCC/PWR/SYSCFG config registers + fold the tz-2 lock over them — the readback is only meaningful once NS cannot rewrite the clock tree), #642 (bound the unbounded RCC/HSI48 waits — same function, land together), #46 (pin RM0456 option-byte values into the read-back verifier), #296/#240/#231 (rainbow FI sweeps on the sign chain — the window should be added to those sweeps), #401/#301 BENCH-4 (the µ-Glitch-shape EMFI campaign that would exercise this), #805 (global RDI jitter — blocked on the CLAUDE.md 'no software PRNG' contract; the proposal's per-site `wait_random` does not hit that contract). (g) Important design constraint from #835 (priority:critical, open): the recently added halt-on-FI-anomaly sink was judged net-negative by two reviewers — spurious halts, retained secrets in SRAM (bare wfe), and a durable page-124 PIN-budget burn when the halt lands after `pin_attempts_bump`'s flash commit. 'Over/under-run ⇒ handle_fault' must therefore NOT be a bare halt around gated_unlock/pin_attempts_bump; use the `hash_engine_fault` pattern (zeroize_sensitive_state + barrier + sys_reset) and keep the window off the post-commit pin-attempt path, or it recreates #835 C3. (h) Envelope caveat is confirmed by measured data: pq1 Type-2 cached sign is 6.4-7.2 s with ±1 s target-sum spread (#699), so windows belong on the deterministic sub-blocks (ct_eq of 4008 B, verify, SCP03/CCM unwrap, SAU/GTZC/AIRCR writes), never on the whole sign. Could not check: whether the Trezor firmware tree at /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware has an instruction-timer equivalent (out of scope for this lens), and no GitHub issue text mentions 'timing canary', 'instruction timer', 'AN12912' or 'RP2350' — search returned nothing, so it is untracked as a distinct item.

feasible.reason: The headline mechanism (`fi::TimedWindow`, a cycle-count envelope on a core-clocked timer) does not defend against either prong of the stated threat. (a) Clock faults: pq1 runs HSI16 -> PLL1 (secure/src/hw/rcc.rs:3, :77-81; no HSE, no external clock pin), so classic clock glitching is not a surface, and any PLL/oscillator perturbation induced by voltage/EM advances DWT CYCCNT (or TIM2/3/5) in lockstep with the CPU - the measured cycle count is frequency-invariant by construction, so the window sees nothing. Detecting a clock-domain anomaly needs an INDEPENDENT reference (LSI-clocked LPTIM/RTC ratio check), which the proposal does not propose. (b) Stuck-at/data faults: they do not change block duration, so the window is blind. What the window actually catches is gross duration change (loop truncation, e.g. the ct_eq length faulted to 0 so `subtle` returns equal after 0 iterations) - a real but narrow subclass the proposal never names. Worse, the design is self-defeating: the envelope must absorb the RDI jitter that `wait_random` (secure/src/fi.rs:86) already injects inside these blocks plus ICACHE/flash-wait-state variance, so 1-3-cycle instruction skips vanish inside it; the LPC55 CDOG analogy only works for deterministic straight-line code with tight bounds, which is exactly what RDI removes. Realisability is also wrong as written: (1) DWT is deliberately unlocked and handed to NS at secure/src/main.rs:4263-4273 (`DSCSR.CDS`, LAR unlocked) and consumed by nonsecure/src/bench_key_speed.rs:35 - using it as the secure reference contradicts an existing design choice; (2) the proposed `wait_random` before the rcc.rs and sau.rs readbacks is impossible at those call sites - `hw::rng::init()` is deliberately deferred until after `sau::init()`/GTZC (main.rs:1193 rcc, :1220 comment, :1351 sau, :1384 rng), so there is no TRNG when either init runs; (3) the gated_unlock->SE verdict and SCP03/CCM unwrap blocks contain I2C round trips with OPTIGA busy/retry and SE050 WTX latency variance of orders of magnitude, so a cycle envelope there is a reliability bug, not a defence. Parts (2) and (3) (post-switch PLL readback, second voted pass over SAU/GTZC/AIRCR) are sound cheap cost-raisers but are a different, S-cost item, and even they only catch a fault that skips the write; an attacker moves to the compare, which the sentinel makes a second-fault target - it raises cost, it does not prevent.
feasible.corrections: Keep as a re-scoped S-cost item: (i) a post-RNG 'config attestation' pass that re-reads RCC_CFGR1/PLL1CFGR/PLL1DIVR and SAU_RBAR/RLAR + GTZC SECCFGRx + AIRCR with `wait_random` + `read_volatile_voted` + `check_true_into_sentinel`, placed AFTER `hw::rng::init()` (main.rs:1384) rather than inside rcc::init/sau::init where no TRNG exists; the existing single-pass F6 `verify_or_halt` (sau.rs:401-409) stays as the pre-RNG first pass. (ii) If a timing window is wanted at all, restrict it to deterministic blocks with no I2C and no internal RDI (the 4008-B ct_eq and C10 verify-before-release), measure the envelope on silicon per release (LTO/opt-s layout and ICACHE state shift cycle counts; it is not computable at build time), and run it off an already-secured TIM (TIM2/TIM3 are in SAU SECCFGR; TIM5 is 32-bit and would need a new SECCFGR bit) or the banked secure SysTick - never the NS-shared DWT. Treat it as catching loop-truncation only, not clock or stuck-at faults. (iii) For actual clock-anomaly detection, the honest U585 option is a two-clock ratio check (LSI-clocked LPTIM vs core cycles) - a different proposal; note that it needs no hardware change but LSI tolerance (+-5%) bounds its sensitivity. (iv) Drop the SE-verdict/SCP03/CCM targets. (v) Flash cost is small (hundreds of bytes) and does not meaningfully worsen the 76,949-B ui-px overrun, but every envelope constant becomes a per-release silicon re-measurement step.
